summary: An ordinary common table expression names an intermediate query for use within one statement.
syntax: WITH name AS (SELECT ...) SELECT ... FROM name
documentation: An ordinary common table expression names an intermediate query for use within one statement. It can separate aggregation from later filtering without creating a permanent database table.
inputs: A named SELECT and the statement that uses its results.
returns: The final query result; the CTE name exists only for that statement.
caution: A CTE is not persistent storage. Do not assume that naming one guarantees a particular materialization or performance strategy.
scenarios: Separate per-customer invoice totals from follow-up rules.
Make a multi-stage sales report easier to inspect.
Reuse an intermediate classification within a single query.
title: Find customers above a paid total
problem: From payments(id INTEGER, customer TEXT, cents INTEGER, paid INTEGER), total cents only where paid = 1, grouped by customer. Return customer and total_cents for totals >= 1000, ordered by customer. cents are non-NULL integers. Unpaid rows must not affect totals.
goal: Use WITH common table expression or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Create a paid_totals CTE, then filter its total_cents column.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT or WITH query against the supplied tables.
SELECT 1;
